Consistent maidens Thats My Boy Luke and Triple Force are feared most as they've been in good form at this venue of late off similar ratings.

Ben Haslam has a good record at this venue and has a couple of ex Irish making their first starts over hurdles for the yard. Jolie Coeur Allen may do the best of his pair.

Horn Cape hinted at a revival last time travelling well before hanging under pressure on ground much quicker than ideal. He's slipping down the weights and if the forecast rain arrives he holds solid claims. HURRICANE ALI has proven inconsistent of late but he has been racing over a variety of trips and will find this more suitable. When he was last seen over a distance close to this he was an unlucky loser over hurdles and he has dropped to a very good mark so can make a winning chase debut. Disco Annie is yet to build on a promising debut but is also feared if allowed an easy lead here.

selections.comment: Great Chieftain shapes as a progressive 4yo. The gelding landed a Class 3 handicap by 2l off 83 at Newmarket last time, running on strongly, hails from an in-form yard, has an eyecatching jockey booking, acts on the ground, suits the trip and goes on a galloping track. He ticks plenty of boxes off a 6lb rise for that win on the Rowley Mile and is one of the lower-weighted runners. NO RETREAT could be up to giving weight all round. Very lightly raced, having had only six starts previously, this is another 4yo open to improvement. Beaten a neck at Meydan last time out, he returns off a break and a gelding op on this first start for George Scott. Another who ticks plenty of boxes here, he acts on the ground, gets further, has been sent off favourite on five of those six starts and goes well fresh. The gelding is yet to finish out of the first three and is bang in the mix off a 3lb rise. Dashing Darcey could outrun his price. There were excuses when denied a clear run and hampered in the Lincoln last time out and the 4yo was in good form before that. Although unproven on fast ground, his only attempt on good to firm was in the Britannia at Royal Ascot, which is easy to forgive the colt.

selections.comment: King Casper travelled strongly at Newmarket last time out on handicap debut, Transparent in second, scoring readily off a mark of 81. The colt acts on the track, suits quick ground, shapes as a progressive 3yo and is a contender off a 9lb rise for that win upped in class. TEROOMM is another runner who could improve markedly on handicap debut. The Roger Varian-trained colt was sent off at odds-on when scoring in maiden and then novice company, the latter under a penalty, in April. It looks significant that his powerful connections have chosen a Class 2 event for the colt's handicap bow given Raadobarg, their 2021 winner of this race, was sent to the Britannia Stakes at Royal Ascot on his next start. Dixieland Blues is another unexposed colt with potential for improvement and must be held in some regard at home making his handicap debut in a Class 2 event. While yet to race on turf, his half-brother was a dual Group 2 winner over 8f on turf, and represents a yard that demand respect.

selections.comment: If RUNNING LION recaptures her Prix de l'Opera (Group 2) form of last October then she will take all the beating. That is the big if for this filly, as she was frankly disappointing in the Dahlia Stakes (Group 2) on her seasonal return at Newmarket and can throw in blowout runs as well as impressive victories. Despite that, she acts on the ground, will suit the step up in trip, represents the form choice and this drop in class makes her hard to oppose. Secret Satire could outrun her price. Ahead of the selection in the Dahlia Stakes off a long absence, she's not without a chance based on last season's Musidora Stakes (Group 3) victory and Belmont Oaks Invitational Stakes (Grade 1) fifth in the States on firm ground prior to that Newmarket return. Although Diamond Rain is on a retrieval mission, the filly is very lightly raced and could post an improved effort if recapturing her early season form of last year, most notably when landing a 10f Listed event in good style at Newbury on just her second start following a winning debut.

selections.comment: A fascinating renewal of the Betfred Sandy Lane Stakes can go to ARIZONA BLAZE. The selection was impressive when comfortably winning the Prix Sigy (Group 3) at Chantilly over an extended 5f last time out on good to soft, but is versatile trip-wise and going-wise, as he showed when a close-up second in the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf Sprint (Grade 1) over 5f on firm ground at Del Mar last season, and holds strong claims on this return to 6f. Symbol Of Honour travelled strongly when winning the Carnarvon Stakes (Listed) over 6f at Newbury by 2l last week. The gelding acts on the ground, is progressive and rates as a major player from this powerful yard. Big Mojo is an admirably consistent Group-winning sprinter who landed a second Group 3 win on his seasonal return following a wind op. Both wins have come on good to firm and the colt showed his penchant for quick ground when a close-up fourth in the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf Sprint (Grade 1), Arizona Blaze in second, last season. Powerful Glory, the unbeaten winner of the Mill Reef Stakes (Group 2) on just his second start, goes well fresh and this colt is respected on just his third start.

selections.comment: Starlust is the sole Grade 1 winner in the field, having won the Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint at Del Mar last season, and is a major player on seasonal return back over his ideal trip. The obvious concern is the colt carries a penalty for that win, and with Group 1 prizes to contend for at Royal Ascot and at the July meeting at Newmarket, this race may just be needed with those engagements to come. RUMSTAR travelled and then ran on strongly when taking the Palace House Stakes (Group 3) at Newmarket last time out, with three of today's rivals behind him. The 5yo looked an improved performer on the Rowley Mile and can underline that impression here. Faster ground should not be an issue as he is a previous winner on good to firm and handled it in the 2023 Commonwealth Cup (Group 1). Mgheera posted an improved effort when winning Prix de Saint-Georges (Group 3) at Longchamp last time out on her first start for the yard. She's yet to race on good to firm but was a Listed winner on good ground. American Affair is an interesting contender on this Group debut. The 5yo won with a bit in hand in a Class 2 handicap at York last week, looks progressive and his trainer believes he's Group class. That's feasible, and while it may just take a couple of runs in this grade to confirm that impression, it would be no surprise to see another improved performance.

Potential improver Slaudeen may be best of the rest ahead of Learntodiscover.

selections.comment: Marginal preference is for MY MATE ALFIE, whose improved autumn form last season (including two good wins over C&D) gives him leading form prospects and whose reappearance run over 5f last month was encouraging. The return to 6f is a plus and, with race fitness a possibly crucial advantage, he is narrowly preferred to Storm Boy, whose good Australian form makes him a leading player too. This dual Group 1 Ascot entry is treading a similar path to Merchant Navy, a good ex-Australian colt who won this on his debut for Aidan O'Brien in this race in 2018. Lethal Levi is third best ahead of fellow British raider Iberian.

selections.comment: The key horse is clearly FIELD OF GOLD, who would probably have been a narrow winner of the 2,000 Guineas last time had his hand been played a touch sooner. That form sets a very high, clear standard and compensation in the form of Classic success now looks pretty likely. Hotazhell was a good, Group 1-winning 2yo who could well claim second, ahead of Rashabar, another very smart juvenile whose good reappearance effort at Newbury last month showed had trained on well. Unbeaten Cosmic Year - in the same ownership as both Field Of Gold and possible pacesetter Windlord - and Aidan O'Brien's progressive Officer are others to consider.

selections.comment: This may well be between ESHERANN and Propose. Marginal preference is for Esherann, whose debut second at Leopardstown this month reads well in this context and the dam's side of whose pedigree strongly suggests will be better served by this 3f longer trip. Aidan O'Brien won this with newcomer and subsequent St Leger winner Jan Brueghel last year and Irish Derby entry Propose has a decent shout of following up that success for Ballydoyle this time. This last-time-out Dundalk second is the clear main danger ahead of Valorous Power and Rizal.
